summary.intent: Scale back PR 347 (interface merging / scope isolation in the extractor) to a smaller, safer change and get it through CI and review, while coordinating several parallel worker sessions (#347, #353, #367/#348/#349).
summary.outcome: PR 347 was reduced from about +470 to +213/-13 across 6 files and pushed as 093ba504, with the earlier scoped version preserved on wip/interface-scope-structural. Local lint and 1251 tests passed, but CI checks are still queued and Entire Gates is in progress, so there are no review findings yet.

repo: Extractor interface merge rule in visit.rs: two same-name interfaces merge only when both are at module level. Function-body or block interfaces never touch a module-level entry, and a lone local interface keeps its bare-name entry. It uses a `local_depth` counter and a `module_interfaces` key set.
Enums and classes are keyed by bare name and are not scope-isolated. This is documented as a known limitation in docs/edge-cases.md under Resolution.
Local interfaces of the same name in different scopes overwrite each other, and a function-local type alias is not separated from a module-level alias of the same name.
A type-only `.ts` import from React is no longer scanned for components, while a `.ts` file with React value imports is.
Verification gates used: `CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`.
Review findings are read via `entire trail finding list caliper/144 --project gh/orin-dx --freshness current --status open --json`, then each non-Entire check is read by name.

code.finding: Holds the module-level-only interface merge rule, implemented with a local_depth counter and a module_interfaces key set. A later module-level declaration replaces a local one.
Documents the dropped scope-isolation limitation for local interfaces and aliases, and notes that enums and classes are unchanged.

workflow: Preserve a heavier attempt on a wip branch (pushed, no PR) before scaling a PR back, and use a plain push instead of a force push.
Verify in a clean-room worktree to avoid contamination from local state.

Check fail-before by copying the branch's tests onto origin/main source. Four of the eight tests fail there and are real fail-before tests. The other four are regression guards that cannot fail on pre-PR source.
Add tests that assert user-visible rendered output, such as type names never showing `Item@57`, to catch leaks of internal rewriting.
Do not treat a PR as done until the review posts and the checks complete.

friction: GitHub Actions runners did not start any of the 16 queued checks after about 25 minutes of polling, and have been slow for over an hour.
The earlier scoped-key approach leaked internal names such as `Item@57` into rendered types, which forced the scale-back.
The type-specifier test was not isolated on the PR's own intermediate source, so its fail-before status is unknown.
